location: No error found; every step of (i)–(v) checked.
objection: I found no gap. (i) For a residue class mod q/g_d, the count is (x/d^2)/(q/g_d)+θ with |θ|≤1. Here gcd(d^2/g_d, q/g_d)=1, so the class is unique. The bounds |R_1|≤√x and tail ≤2√x are correct, since Σ_{d>D}d^{-2}≤1/⌊D⌋≤2/D. The limit exists, and 0≤g≤1/q follows from Q≤x/q+1. Periodicity follows from g_d|q. (ii) The l-sum is finite, so the interchange is valid, and each count equals q/g_d. (iii) For squarefree d the local factors are coprime, and the Euler product converges absolutely. The three cases p∤q, p||q and p^2|q are handled correctly; p^2|q gives h(p)=0 because n is squarefree. (iv) g_d·g_e/lcm = gcd(gcd(d,e)^2, q) is correct. The parametrisation d=td', e=te' with t, d', e' pairwise coprime and squarefree is a bijection. I(t)=∏_{p∤t}(1−2/p^2), which gives G(t)I(t)/t^4 = A_0 η(t) gcd(t^2,q)/t^2. (v) ∏(1+1/(p^2−2)) = ∏(1−p^{-2})/(1−2p^{-2}) is correct. Every series is absolutely convergent, which justifies the rearrangements. The proof cites no result after 2010. I also checked (ii), (iii), (iv) and (v) numerically for q ∈ {1,2,4,8,9,12,36,72,30}. Up to truncation error (~1e-7 for (ii) and (iv), ~2e-4 for (v), which converges slowly; (iii) asserted to 1e-3), the closed forms agree with the series. A first, slower version of the numerical check was stopped at its time limit without producing output; a faster rewrite ran to completion and produced these results.
other_issues: Cosmetic: (iii) does not say whether 'squarefree n' includes negative n. The argument uses only p^2 ∤ n, so it covers negative squarefree n too.
